//: Composite indexes for this project. This file is now COMPLETE: it lists
both indexes that already exist in restopos-db plus the two the current
Cloud Functions need. Deploying it is therefore additive — it creates what
is missing and deletes nothing.
Why that matters: `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes` reconciles the
ENTIRE set. Any index live in the project but absent here is deleted, and
the CLI refuses non-interactively rather than do that silently. That is why
the earlier attempt failed. Never pass --force to work around it; --force
means 'yes, delete the ones I forgot'.
Two kinds of index are NOT listed here and must not be added:
- single-field indexes (Firestore creates those automatically, in both
directions). loadArchivedRange's client_data/{key}/invoices query is
range + orderBy on `date` alone, so it is already served. A composite
entry with one field is rejected by the CLI outright.
- anything under fieldOverrides. The project has none; the CLI's earlier
reconcile error named only the 2 extra indexes, and it reports missing
field overrides in the same breath when they exist. Re-check the
console's 'Single field' tab before deploying if that ever changes.
zatcaChain: this tenant's chain head and recent invoices.
MISSING in production as of 2026-07-28 — this deploy creates it. Until
then the chain lookup fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION and a till that
was wiped or replaced restarts its ICV sequence instead of continuing
the audited one.
zatcaExport: a date range for one tenant, paged. invoice_number is in
the sort so the cursor is unambiguous — ordering on timestamp alone
would skip invoices sharing a second, which a busy till produces.
MISSING in production as of 2026-07-28. The legacy (seller_vat,
timestamp) index below does NOT cover this: adding a second sort key
changes the index the query needs.
LEGACY — already live (index ID CICAgOjXh4EK). Left from the export
screen back when the browser queried zatca_invoices directly and sorted
on timestamp alone. Nothing runs that query now; it is listed here only
so a deploy does not delete it. Safe to drop from the console once the
index above has finished building.
ORPHAN — already live (index ID CICAgJiUpoMK). No query in any of the
three repos, in any commit, filters or sorts by seller_name; it was
created by hand in the console. It serves nothing else either, because
seller_name sits between seller_vat and timestamp and an index only
answers a query when the leading fields line up with no gaps. Listed
purely so a deploy does not delete it. Safe to drop.
